reflection.hint: The near end is always rigid. Watch the far end.

phase.inPhase: Velocity and pressure are IN phase
phase.outOfPhase: Velocity and pressure are 180° OUT of phase

screenSummary.playArea: A pipe lies across the play area with a chain of air particles inside it. Below the pipe, two graphs trace the particle displacement and the acoustic pressure along its length. The near end of the pipe is rigid; the far end is either closed or open.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a button that launches a pulse, a control for the far end of the pipe, a checkbox that shows both far ends at once for comparison, playback controls with slow motion, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Launch a pulse and watch what the far end does to it.

currentDetails.atRest: The pipe is at rest. No pulse has been launched.
currentDetails.travellingToward: A pulse is travelling toward the far end of the pipe.
currentDetails.reflecting: The pulse is reflecting off the far end.
currentDetails.nearReflecting: The pulse is reflecting off the rigid near end.
currentDetails.travellingBack: The reflected pulse is travelling back toward the near end.
currentDetails.closedResult: Reflected from the closed end, the displacement pulse has flipped upside down while the pressure pulse has not.
currentDetails.openResult: Reflected from the open end, the displacement pulse is still upright while the pressure pulse has flipped.

screenSummary.playArea: A pipe of air particles oscillating back and forth along its axis, with a movable reference point carrying a displacement arrow and a velocity arrow. Below the pipe, graphs trace displacement, velocity and pressure along its length.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a direction control for the wave, a wavelength control, a checkbox showing the equations, playback controls with slow motion, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Reverse the direction of travel and watch what happens to the velocity and pressure curves.

currentDetails.forward: The wave travels toward the far end. Velocity and pressure are in phase: the air moves fastest toward the far end exactly where it is most compressed.
currentDetails.backward: The wave travels toward the near end. Velocity and pressure are 180 degrees out of phase: the air moves fastest toward the far end exactly where it is most rarefied.

screenSummary.playArea: A pipe whose two ends can each be closed or open, driven at one end. Inside, a standing wave in displacement and pressure, with markers on the nodes and antinodes. Beside it, a ladder of the harmonics this pipe can sound.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a termination control for the pipe ends, broad and fine drive frequency sliders, a ladder of harmonics to snap to, a pipe length control, a checkbox for the node markers, playback controls with slow motion, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Choose a termination, then sweep the frequency to find a resonance — or snap straight to a harmonic.

currentDetails.atResonance: The pipe is at resonance on harmonic {{harmonic}}, at {{frequency}} hertz. A standing wave fills the pipe.
currentDetails.offResonance: The pipe is off resonance at {{frequency}} hertz, between harmonics. Very little standing wave forms.
currentDetails.silent: The driver is off and the pipe is ringing down.

screenSummary.playArea: A pipe set up as one of four instruments, with its standing wave inside, beside a bar chart of the harmonics that pipe can sound.
screenSummary.controlArea: The control area has a control that selects the instrument, playback controls with slow motion, and a Reset All button.
screenSummary.interactionHint: Compare the flute with the clarinet: same length, but not the same harmonics.

currentDetails.allHarmonics: {{instrument}} is open at both ends, so it sounds every harmonic of {{frequency}} hertz.
currentDetails.oddHarmonics: {{instrument}} is stopped at one end, so it sounds only the odd harmonics of {{frequency}} hertz — an octave below an open pipe of the same length.
